decisions.check_result: Re-read every trace and evidence line. dispatch_alerts (backend/app.py:330-356) sends one actuator command per MEDIO/ALTO event (348/350) and one send_photo per upload (356), with no cooldown, count limit or use of LEVEL_COOLDOWN/_last_alert (359-372), which the live path uses to avoid saturating the shared sinks. The docstring at line 334 shows chat flooding was an intended concern, but nothing limits it across uploads. Event count is bounded only by video time/5 s, and video time depends on container fps (engine.py:62, 76, 85). Each ON resets offAt (wokwi/sketch.ino:58). A small upload with a stable person plus hands_up (score 4) yields MEDIO, so repeated uploads post uploader-chosen frames to the shared chat far above the live rate. This is an authorised resident bypassing an anti-flood restriction enforced on the sibling path for the same shared effect, not self-impact. The flood effect is a runtime claim that cannot be confirmed without execution, and whether Telegram throttling drops other residents' alerts is a third-party fact. I removed the event-loop-blocking claim from the root cause: it belongs to the separate fingerprint backend/app.py:analyze:blocking-video-analysis-on-event-loop. I corrected trace and evidence lines (added 334) and made the local plan exact.

Verified that _last_alert (backend/app.py:360) is one module-level dict keyed only by level, and that the check-and-set at 370-372 returns before both the actuator and Telegram calls for any later same-level live event from any camera. backend/Dockerfile:25 runs a single uvicorn process, so every user shares this budget. Scoring arithmetic matches config.yaml and threat_scoring.py: person 1 + loitering 2 (wall-clock 15 s) + manos_arriba 3 = 6 = ALTO, and person + loitering = 3 = MEDIO (daytime, no restricted zone). LiveSession allows one event every 5 s per session (engine.py:146), so one resident can keep both windows occupied with their own frames. The sink is shared, so the attacker's ALTOs still sound the siren half the time; the victim-specific loss is mainly Telegram evidence and siren activations in the window's off phase. That is a real one-principal-suppresses-another effect, not only a quality bug. It was not confirmed because suppression is runtime behaviour (no execution allowed), and multiple live camera owners on one backend is a deployment fact. Lines were re-verified, and the Dockerfile evidence and a deployment plan were added.

Verified that analyze_video uses the engine-level self.scorer (engine.py:46, 83), never reset, while LiveSession builds its own (122). The analyze handler calls analyze_video synchronously with no await inside it (backend/app.py:603) on a single-process server, so analyses cannot interleave: each starts with exactly the state the previous one left. presence_start is set only when None (threat_scoring.py:54-55), so a video ending with presence first seen at video time P makes the next video's continuously present person score loiter_time = t - P, losing the 2 loitering points until t >= P + 15 or until presence breaks. With the committed config (no zone, daytime), MEDIO 3 drops to BAJO 1 (no event, no dispatch) and ALTO 6 drops to MEDIO 4 (WARN instead of siren); at sensitive hours the drop to BAJO does not occur. Inflation via the carried history has no comparable effect, and negative loitering inflation is impossible. The effect crosses users and communities but depends on ordering and on runtime detections, so it remains needs_validation. The fps manipulation is not required (an ordinary 60 s video works). I rewrote the local plan with a deterministic stub detector and worked expected values (events at 18, 24 and 30 s on a fresh engine; none after A).
